title: Space Coast infrastructure delivery, license status, and utilization
question: Which Space Coast plans, licenses, and capital programs convert into accepted infrastructure, available missions, safe operation, and sustained utilization?
why_it_matters: An operating corridor can still contain unresolved site licenses, constrained range and utilities, incomplete capital projects, and unmeasured local or environmental outcomes.
current_support: FTFN now adds FAA cumulative and annual commercial-space operations plus NASA 2025 station logistics as national operating comparators.
missing_evidence: formal current Shuttle Landing Facility license disposition
named state capital awards, contracts, construction, and acceptance
operator and mission licenses tied to infrastructure use
range availability, delay, incident, and utilization data
utility, resilience, workforce, housing, and environmental outcomes
likely_source_types: NASA or Space Force project record
Space Florida contract, audit, or facility record
mission, safety, utilization, and local outcome data
candidate_records: Shuttle Landing Facility renewal, replacement, lapse, or disposition
SLC-40 license modification and landing-zone construction
named FDOT spaceport project agreement and acceptance
KSC master-plan project budget and construction trail
range utilization, mission delay, safety, and resilience records
next annual observation with unchanged method and denominator
machine-readable revision history and data dictionary
asset-, facility-, agency-, carrier-, operator-, or mission-level outcomes
next_action: Resolve the Shuttle Landing Facility license record first, then follow named master-plan, environmental, state-capital, and mission records through construction, acceptance, operation, and outcomes.

named_records: FAA LC-39A Starship Record of Decision
latest_review.stage_result: Eight additional records close one physical asset's opening and one coordinated operating event while adding a final environmental decision, facility upgrades, program delivery rules, and a planned services acquisition. Mission licensing, repeat performance, utilization, and outcomes remain open.
latest_review.stop_rule: Do not treat a site listing, master plan, environmental decision, funding handbook, facility upgrade, procurement plan, one operating event, or one operational asset as a current mission license, corridor readiness, safe performance trend, or sustained utilization.

notes: Phase 55Z preserves the dated Space Coast license check and does not convert national cadence into site-specific authorization, utilization, or local outcomes. Phase 56A adds multi-period official series; only domain-relevant observations should be used in a specific gap analysis.
